Section  151A,  read with section  148,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment  - Faceless assessment of (Issue of notice) - Assessment year  2018-19  - Assessee filed petition challenging validity of reassessment notice issued to it - It was noted that impugned notice issued under section 148 and order of same date under section 148A(d) were issued by Jurisdictional Assessing Officer and not under mandatory faceless mechanism as per provisions of section 151A - High Court held that for a notice to be validly issued under section 148, Assessing Officer would be required to comply with provisions of section 151A, so as to adhere to faceless mechanism, as notified by Central Government by notification dated 29-3-2022 - Further, since impugned order and notices issued by Assessing Officer were not in compliance with scheme notified by Central Government implementing provisions of section 151A, impugned reassessment notice issued to assessee was to be set aside - Whether there was a gross delay of 248 days in filing SLP and same had not been satisfactorily explained by revenue - Held, yes - Whether even otherwise instant court see no reason to interfere with impugned order passed by High Court, thus, SLP filed by revenue was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section 149, read with sections 148 and 148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3 of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issuance of notice (Period of limitation) - Assessee filed Writ Petitions stating that issues in these petitions will be covered by recent judgment of this Court in Godrej Industries Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2024] 160 taxmann.com 13 (Bombay) wherein it was held that validity of a notice must be judged on basis of law existing as on date on which notice was issued under section 148; in terms of Finance Act, 2021 no notice under section 148 for assessment year 2014-15 could be issued on or after 1-4-2021 based on first proviso to section 149 and, thus, impugned reopening notice issued on 31-7-2022 for assessment year 2014-15 was barred by limitation - Revenue agreed with this submission - High Court by impugned order held that orders passed under section 148A(d) and notices issued under section 148 in respective petitions were to be quashed and set aside –On SLP filed by revenue it was found that SLP was covered by judgement of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 (SC) - Whether therefore, assessee will be governed by reasons discussed in said Judgment and Assessing Officers will dispose of objections in terms of law laid down by this Court and assessee will be at liberty to pursue all rights and remedies in accordance with law, save and except for issues concluded in Judgment - Held, yes - Whether in view of above, SLP filed by revenue was to be disposed of - Held, yes [Paras 2, 3 and 4] [Partly in favour of revenue]

Section  148,  read with section  148A,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / section  280,  read with section  281,  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 - Income escaping assessment – Issue of notice for (Reassessment) - Assessment years  2013-14 and 2014-15  - Assessees filed writ petitions challenging reassessment actions for AYs 2013-14 and 2014-15 - In one, reopening was under regime prevailing prior to Finance Act, 2021, and in other, initiation was under section 148A(b) - It was noted that recorded reasons for reopening were based solely on surveys conducted in 2007 and 2019 on various constituents of GE Group in India - High Court held that since reasons for reassessment did not allude to any facts specific to assessment years in question and merely reiterated survey findings, notices under section 148 were to be quashed - Whether there was gross delay of 267 days in filing SLP which had not been satisfactorily explained by revenue, even otherwise, there was no good ground to interfere with impugned order passed by High Court and, thus, SLP was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section  148  read with sections  132  and  281B  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and sections  31  and  62  of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Issue of notice for  (IBC matter) - Assessment year  2016-17  - A search and seizure operation was conducted against assessee under section 132 - Bank of India filed an application under section 7 of Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) before NCLT, which admitted Corporate Debtor into Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) - NCLT permitted Income Tax Department to conduct assessment proceedings for AYs 2013-14 to 2018-19, directing it to file claims with Resolution Professional - NCLT approved Resolution Plan submitted by Committee of Creditors, thereby concluding CIRP - Subsequently, department issued an assessment order for AYs 2013-14 to 2019-20 and appealed to NCLAT for inclusion of its claims, but appeal was dismissed - During pendency, department issued a notice under section 148 to reopen assessment for Assessment Year 2016-17 - It was noted that in Ghanashyam Mishra & Sons (P.) Ltd. v. Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Co. Ltd. [2021] 126 taxmann.com 132/166 SCL 237 (SC), Supreme Court held that once NCLT approves a Resolution Plan, all past dues are extinguished - Further, assessee had an even stronger position as NCLT's order merged with NCLAT's dismissal, achieving finality under section 62 of IBC - High Court held that in view of foregoing reasons and considering decision of Apex Court in facts of case, notice issued under section 148 was not tenable in eyes of law and was accordingly, quashed and set aside - Whether court was not inclined to interfere with impugned order pass by High Court and, thus, SLP was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 3 and 4] [In favour of assessee]

Section  148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, read with section  31 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 -  Income escaping assessment -  Issue of notice for (Illustrations) - High Court by impugned order held that where pursuant to resolution plan approved by NCLT, all claims of Governmental Authorities including income-tax dues were to stand fully and finally discharged and settled, notice under section 148 issued by revenue to assessee-company after approval of resolution plan by NCLT for a period prior to closing date, was invalid and bad in law - Whether since there was gross delay of 250 days in filing SLP by revenue and delay had not been satisfactorily explained, SLP was to dismissed on ground of delay as well as on merits - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section 149, read with sections 148 and 148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3 of the Taxation and other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issue of notice (Illustrations) - Assessment year 2013-14 - Assessee filed writ petition challenging reopening notice alongwith order passed under section 148A(d) on ground that the same were bad in law and without jurisdiction - High Court by impugned order held that reassessment notice issued for assessment year 2013-14, under old regime after expiry of six years limitation period were barred by limitation - Whether SLP was to be disposed of in terms of judgment of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 (SC) - Held, yes [Para 2] [Partly in favour of revenue]INCOME TAX : Where High Court by impugned order held that reassessment notice issued for assessment year 2013-14, under old regime after expiry of six years limitation period were barred by limitation, SLP filed against impugned order was to be disposed of in terms of judgment of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 (SC)

Section 149, read with sections 148 and 148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section 3 of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 and Article 142 of the Constitution of India, 1950 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issuance of notice - Assessment years 2016-17 and 2017-18 - A notice dated 28-6-2021 under unamended section 148 was issued upon assessee in respect of relevant assessment year 2017-18 - Similarly, a notice dated 30-6-2021 under unamended section 148 was issued upon assessee in respect of relevant assessment year 2016-17 - Pursuant to judgment of Supreme Court in case of Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC), revenue issued another notice under section 148A(b) dated 20-5-2022 for assessment year 2017-18 - Assessee contended that reassessment proceedings triggered against it were time-barred as limitation period of three years qua relevant assessment years had expired - High Court by impugned order held that reassessment notice issued on or after 1-4-2021 under unamended section 148 would be deemed to have been issued under substituted section 148A(b) and revenue could not have issued another notice under section 148A(b) for assessment year 2017-18 - High Court further held that since alleged escaped income was less than Rs. 50 lakhs, impugned notices issued between 1-4-2021 and 30-6-2021, by which time limitation of three years under section 149(1)(a) had already expired, were barred by limitation - Whether SLP was to be disposed of in terms of judgment of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC) - Held, yes [Paras 3] [Partly in favour of revenue]INCOME TAX : Where High Court by impugned order held that alleged escaped income was less than Rs. 50 lakhs, impugned, reopening notices dated 30-6-2021 and 28-6-2021 under unamended section 148 issued upon assessee in respect of assessment years 2016-17 and 2017-18 respectively being issued after three years were barred by limitation as per section 149, SLP filed against impugned order was to be disposed of in terms of judgment of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC)

Section  149,  read with sections  148  and  153C, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / Section  282  , read with section  280  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice  (Reassessment) - Assessment year  2016-17  - A search was conducted in case of SMC Group alleging that group entities had obtained accommodation entries and that assessee had availed a loan from a suspected shell entity - Accordingly, Assessing Officer initiated proceedings under section 148A - Assessing Officer passed order under section 148A(d) and issued notice under section 148 on 30-08-2024 - It was noted that, clause (a) of proviso to section 148A was inapplicable as assessee was not one of entities that was searched - Further, there was no material on record, to establish that books of account, documents, other material or assets had been found, which either belonged to assessee or contained information pertaining to assessee, during search conducted on SMC Group - High Court held that condition as stipulated under clause (c) of proviso to section 148A was not satisfied and this was not a case where a notice under section 153C could have been issued - Further, question whether a notice could be issued under section 148 was required to be determined on basis whether such notice could have been issued under provisions as in force prior to 01-04-2021 - Additionally, since notice was issued beyond period of six years from end of relevant assessment year, said notice was barred by limitation in terms of first proviso to section 149(1) - Whether since SLP was squarely covered by judgment of SC in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 (SC), assessee will be governed by reasons discussed in said judgment and, thus, SLP filed by revenue was to be disposed of - Held, yes [Paras 2 to 4] [Partly in favour of revenue]

Section  148, read with sections  143(3) and  147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment -  Issue of notice for (Reassessment) - Assessment years  2016-17 and 2017-18 - Assessee had filed its return of income declaring NIL income which was accepted in assessment under section 143(3) - Thereafter, Assessing Officer received an information from credible sources that during a survey action under section 133A on JK bank it was noticed that assessee was one of beneficiaries who had entered into transaction of Rs. 62.77 crores in form of inward and outward remittances - On basis of aforesaid information, he issued a notice under section 148 on ground that income of assessee had escaped assessment to tune of Rs. 62.77 crores within meaning of section 147 - It was observed that assessee had produced all material before Assessing Officer during course of regular assessment in form of details of bank accounts along with bank statement of JK Bank, details of exchange, difference/net loss in foreign exchange transaction and translations along with copies of ledger account of exchange difference, details of expenditure in foreign currency, copy of Form-15CA etc. - High Court held that since impugned notice was issued on change of opinion on part of Assessing Officer only on borrowed satisfaction without there being any fresh tangible material to come to prima facie conclusion that income had escaped assessment, same was liable to be quashed and set aside - In instant SLP, Whether since there was inordinate delay of 198 days and 79 days in filing/refiling SLP which has not been satisfactorily explained - Held, yes - Whether instant court found no good reason to interfere with impugned order passed by High Court and accordingly SLP filed by revenue was to be dismissed on ground of delay as well as merits - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : SLP dismissed against order of High Court that where Assessing Officer issued a notice under section 148 on basis of information that assessee had entered into transaction of Rs. 62.77 crores in form of inward and outward remittances, since assessee had produced all details of foreign remittance during course of regular assessment, impugned notice issued on change of opinion and only on borrowed satisfaction without there being any fresh tangible material was quashed and set aside

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Notice for - Assessment year 1984-85 - Whether simply preparing notice under section 148 but keeping it on file past limitation period does not tantamount to issuing same, and, thus, such notice is bad in law - Held, yes

Section 148, read with section 143, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for - Assessment years 1989-90 to 1996-97 - Whether having regard to amendment made by Finance Act, 2006 inserting proviso to section 148, in respect of return filed between period 1-10-1991 and 30-9-2005 pursuant to notice issued under section 148, proceedings under section 148 would not be hit by limitation on issuance of notice under section 143(2); in such case only limitation, that has to be seen to confer validity to proceedings under section 148, would be time-limit given under section 153(2) for making assessment, reassessment, recomputation and nothing beyond - Held, yes

Section  149,  read with section  148,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice  (General) - Assessment year  2016-17  - Assessee challenged notice issued under section 148 - It was noted that period of six years for relevant assessment year 2016-17, expired on 31-3-2022 - High Court held that since notice had been issued thereafter on 30-8-2024, same was barred by limitation - Whether there was gross delay of 411 days in filing SLP which had not been satisfactorily explained by revenue, even otherwise, there was no good ground to interfere with impugned order passed by High Court and, thus, SLP was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section  148, read with sections  143(3) and  147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment -  Issue of notice for (Reassessment) - Assessment years  2016-17 and 2017-18 - Assessee had filed its return of income declaring NIL income which was accepted in assessment under section 143(3) - Thereafter, Assessing Officer received an information from credible sources that during a survey action under section 133A on JK bank it was noticed that assessee was one of beneficiaries who had entered into transaction of Rs. 62.77 crores in form of inward and outward remittances - On basis of aforesaid information, he issued a notice under section 148 on ground that income of assessee had escaped assessment to tune of Rs. 62.77 crores within meaning of section 147 - It was observed that assessee had produced all material before Assessing Officer during course of regular assessment in form of details of bank accounts along with bank statement of JK Bank, details of exchange, difference/net loss in foreign exchange transaction and translations along with copies of ledger account of exchange difference, details of expenditure in foreign currency, copy of Form-15CA etc. - High Court held that since impugned notice was issued on change of opinion on part of Assessing Officer only on borrowed satisfaction without there being any fresh tangible material to come to prima facie conclusion that income had escaped assessment, same was liable to be quashed and set aside - In instant SLP, Whether since there was inordinate delay of 198 days and 79 days in filing/refiling SLP which has not been satisfactorily explained - Held, yes - Whether instant court found no good reason to interfere with impugned order passed by High Court and accordingly SLP filed by revenue was to be dismissed on ground of delay as well as merits - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Notice to dead person) - Pursuant to summons issued in name of assessee's father under section 131(1A), assessee brought to notice of revenue authorities that his father had already died - Despite knowing said fact, Assessing Officer issued notice in name of assessee's father under section 148 seeking to reopen assessment - Assessee thus filed instant petition contending that impugned notice was without any jurisdiction which was issued against a dead person - High Court held that no valid notice could be issued against a dead person and, thus impugned notice was required to be quashed and set aside - Whether, on facts, SLP filed against order of High Court was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Para 2][In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : Where High Court set aside reassessment proceedings on ground that no valid notice under section 148 could be issued against a dead person, SLP filed against said order was to be dismissed

Section 148A, read with sections 148 and 149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section 3 of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 – Income escaping assessment - Conducting inquiry, providing opportunity before issue of notice (Limitation period) - Assessment year 2013-14 - Assessee challenged notice issued under section 148 on ground that it was time-barred as per newly substituted section 149(1)(a)  (b)- Revenue contended that time limit for issuing notice was extended until 30-6-2021, was extended by section 3 of TOLA read with Notification No. 20/2021 dated 31-3-2021, and Notification No. 38/2021 dated 27-4-2021, until 30-6-2021 - High Court by impugned order held that since time period for issuance of reassessment notice stood extended until 30-6-2021 and income alleged escaped income was over Rs. 50 lakhs, first proviso of section 149 would not be applicable - It further held that even without benefit of Instruction No. 01/2022 reopening notice issued on 23-6-2021 was within limitation - Whether since no interference was called for in order passed by High Court, SLP filed by assessee was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Para 3] [In favour of revenue]INCOME TAX : SLP dismissed against order of High Court that since time period for issuance of reassessment notice for assessment year 2013-14 stood extended by section 3 of TOLA until 30-6-2021 and alleged escaped income of assessee was beyond Rs. 50 lakh, first proviso of section 149 (as amended by Finance Act, 2021) would not be attracted and thus reassessment proceeding initiated during time limit extended by TOLA was not barred by limitation

Section  149 , read with sections  148  and  148A , of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issuance of notice (Validity of notice) - Assessment year 2014-15 - High Court held that since period of six years from end of relevant assessment year expired on 31-3-2021, notice issued under section 148 on 30-8-2024 to assessee was barred by limitation - Whether there was gross delay of 327 days in filing SLP which had not been satisfactorily explained, even otherwise court found no good reason to interfere with impugned order passed by High Court and, thus, SLP was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section  149 , read with sections  148  and  148A , of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issuance of notice (Validity of notice) - Assessment year 2014-15 - High Court held that since period of six years from end of relevant assessment year expired on 31-3-2021, notice issued under section 148 on 30-8-2024 to assessee was barred by limitation - Whether there was gross delay of 327 days in filing SLP which had not been satisfactorily explained, even otherwise court found no good reason to interfere with impugned order passed by High Court and, thus, SLP was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : SLP dismissed against order of High Court that where for relevant assessment year 2014-15, period of six years from end of relevant assessment year expired on 31-3-2021, notice issued under section 148 on 30-8-2024 to assessee was barred by limitation

Section  149,  read with sections  148  and  148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3  of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 -  Income Escaping Assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice  (Period of limitation) - Assessee filed writ petitions stating that issues in these petitions were covered by recent judgment of this Court in Godrej Industries Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2024] 160 taxmann.com 13 (Bombay) wherein it was held that validity of a notice must be judged on basis of law existing as on date on which notice was issued under section 148; in terms of Finance Act, 2021 no notice under section 148 for assessment year 2014-15 could be issued on or after 1-4-2021 based on first proviso to section 149 and, thus, impugned reopening notice issued on 31-7-2022 for assessment year 2014-15 was barred by limitation - Revenue agreed with this submission - High Court held that orders passed under section 148A(d) and notices issued under section 148 in respective petitions were to be quashed and set aside - Whether SLP was squarely covered by judgment of SC in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 (SC), assessee will be governed by reasons discussed in said judgment and, thus, SLP filed by revenue was to be disposed of - Held, yes [Paras 2 and 3] [Partly in favour of revenue]

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Validity of notice) - Assessment year 2001-02 - In appellate proceedings, Tribunal noted that notice under section 148 was not issued at correct address because address given in notice was not last known address of assessee - Tribunal further opined that mere fact that assessee had participated in reassessment proceedings despite not having been issued or served with notice under section 148 in accordance with law would not constitute a waiver of said jurisdictional requirement - Thus, Tribunal set aside reassessment order - High Court upheld Tribunal's order - Revenue filed SLP against High Court's order; however, sought permission to withdraw same due to low tax effect - Whether, on facts, SLP filed by revenue was to be dismissed as withdrawn - Held, yes [Para 3] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX: Where High Court upheld Tribunal's order setting aside reassessment proceedings on ground that notice under section 148 was not issued at last known address of assessee, SLP filed against said order was to be dismissed due to low tax effect

Section  149,  read with sections  148  and  148A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3  of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice  (Period of limitation) - Assessee filed writ challenging reopening notice and stated that issue was covered by High Court's decision in Godrej Industries Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2024] 160 taxmann.com 13 (Bombay) - Revenue agreed to said claim - High Court held that validity of a notice must be judged on basis of law existing as on date on which notice was issued under section 148 and impugned order passed under section 148A(d) and notice issued under section 148 were to be quashed on ground of limitation - Whether instant SLP was covered by Judgment of this Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/ 301 Taxman 238 (SC) and thus assessing officers will dispose of objections in terms of law laid down by Court and thereafter, assessee, if aggrieved, would be at liberty to pursue all rights and remedies in accordance with law - Held, yes - Whether SLP filed by revenue was to be disposed of - Held, yes [Paras 2 to 4] [Partly in favour of revenue]

Section 149, read with sections 148 and 148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section  3 of the Taxation and other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issue of notice (Illustrations) - Assessment year 2013-14 - Assessee filed writ petition challenging reopening notice alongwith order passed under section 148A(d) on ground that the same were bad in law and without jurisdiction - High Court by impugned order held that reassessment notice issued for assessment year 2013-14, under old regime after expiry of six years limitation period were barred by limitation - Whether SLP was to be disposed of in terms of judgment of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 (SC) - Held, yes [Para 2] [Partly in favour of revenue]

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Validity of notice) - Assessment year 2001-02 - In appellate proceedings, Tribunal noted that notice under section 148 was not issued at correct address because address given in notice was not last known address of assessee - Tribunal further opined that mere fact that assessee had participated in reassessment proceedings despite not having been issued or served with notice under section 148 in accordance with law would not constitute a waiver of said jurisdictional requirement - Thus, Tribunal set aside reassessment order - High Court upheld Tribunal's order - On SLP, revenue stated that this petition be dismissed on ground of low tax effect as being covered by Circular No. 17 of 2019 dated 8-8-2019 issued by Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance - Whether in view of statement so made, this Special Leave Petition was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Para 2] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : SLP dismissed against order of High Court upholding Tribunal's order setting aside reassessment proceedings on ground that notice under section 148 was not issued at last known address of assessee

Section  149,  read with section  148,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income Escaping Assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice  (General) - High Court held that where last date for service of notice and initiating proceedings under section 148 under unamended provisions was coming to an end on 31-3-2021 but notices had been issued from office of Department either on 1-4-2021 or on subsequent dates, impugned notices were barred by limitation under sections 148 and 149 - Whether two identical matters arising from High Court has already been dismissed by instant court in Income-tax Officer, National Faceless Assessment Centre Delhi v. Consortium of Institutions of Higher Learning [2025] 177 taxmann.com 196 (SC) and Additional/ Joint/ Deputy/ Assistant Commissioner of Income-tax/ Income-tax Officer v. Anantha Reddy Pannala [2025] 175 taxmann.com 688 (SC), accordingly instant SLP filed by revenue was also to be dismissed [Paras 2 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section 149, read with sections 148 and 148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section 3 of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 and Article 142 of the Constitution of India, 1950 - Income escaping assessment - Time limit for issuance of notice - Assessment years 2016-17 and 2017-18 - A notice dated 28-6-2021 under unamended section 148 was issued upon assessee in respect of relevant assessment year 2017-18 - Similarly, a notice dated 30-6-2021 under unamended section 148 was issued upon assessee in respect of relevant assessment year 2016-17 - Pursuant to judgment of Supreme Court in case of Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC), revenue issued another notice under section 148A(b) dated 20-5-2022 for assessment year 2017-18 - Assessee contended that reassessment proceedings triggered against it were time-barred as limitation period of three years qua relevant assessment years had expired - High Court by impugned order held that reassessment notice issued on or after 1-4-2021 under unamended section 148 would be deemed to have been issued under substituted section 148A(b) and revenue could not have issued another notice under section 148A(b) for assessment year 2017-18 - High Court further held that since alleged escaped income was less than Rs. 50 lakhs, impugned notices issued between 1-4-2021 and 30-6-2021, by which time limitation of three years under section 149(1)(a) had already expired, were barred by limitation - Whether SLP was to be disposed of in terms of judgment of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC) - Held, yes [Paras 3] [Partly in favour of revenue]

Section 151, read with section 148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income Escaping Assessment - Sanction for issue of notice (Specified authority) - High Court by impugned order held that where revenue issued a notice under section 148A(b) to assessee after lapse of more than three years from end of relevant assessment year after obtaining prior approval from Principal Commissioner, since approval was sought from authorities specified in clause (i), as against clause (ii) of section 151, impugned notice and order were to be quashed on ground that there was no approval of specified authority as indicated in section 151(ii), however, liberty was to be given to revenue to commence reassessment proceedings afresh, if deemed necessary, albeit as per law - On SLP filed by revenue it was found that SLP was covered by judgement of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC) - Whether therefore, assessee will be governed by reasons discussed in said Judgment and Assessing Officers will dispose of objections in terms of law laid down by this Court and assessee will be at liberty to pursue all rights and remedies in accordance with law, save and except for issues concluded in Judgment - Held, yes - Whether in view of above, SLP filed by revenue was to be disposed of - Held, yes [Paras 2, 3 and 4][Partly in favour of revenue]

II. Section  148,  read with sections  148A  and  149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment – Issue of notice for (Limitation) - Assessment year  2015-16  - Assessee-company, engaged in business of manufacturing, filed its original return of income - Assessment was completed under section 143(3) - Subsequently, a reopening notice under section 148 was issued on 30-7-2022 - It was noted that as per Supreme Court decision in Rajeev Bansal v. Union of India [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70, reassessment notices pertained to assessment years 2013-14 to 2017-18 could be issued only upto 31-3-2022 and benefit of extension of due date as per TOLA would be applicable only to notices issued between 1-4-2021 to 30-6-2021 - Further, as per section 149 of new regime, time limit for reopening assessments has been reduced from four years to three years - Whether since limitation for assessment year 2015-16 was expiring on 31-3-2022, benefit of TOLA would not be applicable and, thus, notice issued under section 148 on 30-7-2022 was barred by limitation - Held, yes [Para 17] [In favour of assessee]

Section  149,  read with sections  148  and  148A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice  (Scope of) - Assessment year  2016-17  - Assessing Officer issued a notice under section 148 dated 31-8-2024 for relevant assessment year - It was noted that period of six years from end of relevant assessment year expired on 31-3-2023 - High Court held that notice was barred by limitation and was to be set aside - Whether since SLP was squarely covered by judgment of SC in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 (SC), assessee will be governed by reasons discussed in said judgment and, thus, SLP filed by revenue was to be disposed of - Held, yes [Paras 2 and 3] [Partly in favour of revenue]

Section 148, read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Notice of - Assessment years 1971-72 and 1972-73 - Whether, where a valid notice under section 148 had been issued but no assessment had been completed nor were proceedings dropped by the Assessing Officer, he was disentitled to initiate fresh assessment proceedings by issuing another notice under section 148 - Held, yes - Whether assessment completed on the basis of second notice under section 148 would be invalid - Held, yes - Whether, where assessment proceedings initiated on the basis of first notice under section 148 got barred by limitation, they could be revived by issuing fresh notice under section 148 - Held, no

Section  149,  read with section  148,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income Escaping Assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice  (Period of limitation) - Assessment year  2017-18  - Assessee filed petition challenging reopening notice dated 1-5-2024 under section 148A for assessment year 2017-18 - Assessee contended that said notice was issued beyond period of limitation as prescribed in first proviso to section 149(1) - High Court held that in view of decision of Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70 (SC), order and notice issued under section 148 in respect of assessment year 2017-18 was to be set aside - Whether SLP was reported to be beyond time by 320 days, even otherwise, Court did not find sufficient explanation to condone delay and, thus, SLP was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 1 and 2] [In favour of assessee]

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Service of notice) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessing Officer had reopened assessment of assessee and sent notice for service to him through postal department at address contained in his PAN Card, which was returned back by postal department with remark 'left' - Assessee challenged process of reopening of assessment contending that remark of postal department 'left' was totally incorrect, since he had received various communications from Income Tax Department at address contained in PAN card - High Court held that since assessee had not joined postal department to question why remark 'left' was made and Assessing Officer was entitled to proceed on basis of remark of postal department, only on ground of non service of notice, reassessment proceedings could not be terminated - Whether since assessee did not press SLP, same was to be dismissed as not pressed - Held, yes [Para 2] [In favour of revenue]IT: Where Assessing Officer had reopened assessment of assessee and sent notice to him through postal department at address contained in his PAN card, which was returned back with remark 'left', and assessee challenged reopening of assessment contending that remark 'left' was totally incorrect, since assessee had not joined postal department to question why remark 'left' was made, only on ground of non service of notice, reassessment proceedings could not be terminated SLP was dismissed

Section  148, read with section  149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment -  Issue of notice for (Limitation) - Assessment year  2009-10 - Reassessment proceedings were initiated in case of assessee by issuing notice on 15-3-2016 by Assessing Officer - Assessee filed writ petition on ground that on 13-04-2016, for first time, he was served with notice under section 148(1) through his Chartered Accountant and, thus, no notice was issued within period of limitation as prescribed under section 149(1)(b) read with section 148(1) and, therefore, initiation of proceeding for reassessment was barred by limitation - Single Judge allowed writ petition holding that no notice was served to assessee under section 148(1) and service of notice to Chartered Accountant was not service at all - High Court held that had it been a case of revenue that notice was served upon assessee before 31-03-2016, then why they have again issued notice through Chartered Accountant on 13-04-2016 was not understood and, therefore, notice under section 148 issued on 13-04-2016 was after period of limitation, i.e., dated 31-03-2016 - Whether since there was a delay of 327 days in filing Special Leave Petition (SLP) against said order of High Court and explanation rendered for said delay was not satisfactory, SLP was to be dismissed on ground of delay and laches - Held, yes [Para 1] [In favour of assessee]

Section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income escaping assessment - Issue of notice for (Validity of notice) - Assessment year 2001-02 - In appellate proceedings, Tribunal noted that notice under section 148 was not issued at correct address because address given in notice was not last known address of assessee - Tribunal further opined that mere fact that assessee had participated in reassessment proceedings despite not having been issued or served with notice under section 148 in accordance with law would not constitute a waiver of said jurisdictional requirement - Thus, Tribunal set aside reassessment order - High Court upheld Tribunal's order - On SLP, revenue stated that this petition be dismissed on ground of low tax effect as being covered by Circular No. 17 of 2019 dated 8-8-2019 issued by Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance - Whether in view of statement so made, this Special Leave Petition was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Para 2] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars and Notifications : Circular No. 17 of 2019, dated 8-8-2019

Section 68, read with section 148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Cash credit (Reassessment) - Assessment year 2011-12 - Assessee filed its return of income was selected for scrutiny and an assessment order under section 143(3) was passed, making additions under section 68 - Thereafter, a reopening notice was issued on ground that assessee had not disclosed fully and truly all facts and details with regard to trading done through broker and as such, return was processed under section 143(1) and no scrutiny assessment was passed under section 143(3) - It was noted that at time when assessment order under section 143(3) was passed, Assessing Officer was in possession of transaction details through broker and thereby, same could not be made subject matter again to assume jurisdiction under section 148 for reopening of assessment, as same had already been concluded - High Court by impugned order held that reopening notice was nothing but change of opinion and same was not permissible in law - There was gross delay of 185 days in filing SLP - Whether since delay had not been satisfactorily explained and even otherwise, there was no reason to interfere with impugned order passed by High Court, SLP filed by revenue was to be dismissed on ground of delay as well as on merits - Held, yes [Paras 2, 3 and 4][in favour of assessee]

Section 153(1)(c), read with sections 148 and 139, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Reassessment - Time limit for completion of - Assessment year 1979-80 - Assessee filed return in response to notice under section 148 - It later filed a revised return on 30-3-1988, which was processed and assessment was finally completed on 15-3-1989 - Whether, where section 148(1) clearly lays down that notice issued under section 148 shall be deemed to be one issued under section 139(2) and, therefore, all provisions of Act including those of sections 139(5) and 153(1)(c) shall apply accordingly, no sooner returns got filed on 30-3-1988 in terms of section 139(5), Assessing Officer statutorily got benefit of extension of time for making assessment by one more year from said date in accordance with provisions of section 153(1)(c) and order of Commissioner (Appeals) annulling said assessment on ground of limitation had to be reversed - Held, yes

Section 68, read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Cash Credits (Bogus sales) - Assessment year 2014-15 - Assessing Officer completed assessment of assessee under section 143(3) after considering special audit report - Later, Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148 on basis of information received from NSEL that certain amount was outstanding payable by assessee as on termination of trading activity on NSEL and assessee had received said amount against sale of commodities but failed to deliver commodities or repayment of said amount and, thus there was no actual sale done by assessee and by making such bogus sales assessee had benefitted and accordingly there was an escapement of income - High Court by impugned order held that since Assessing Officer issued impugned notice only on basis of information received from NSEL without considering facts on record to effect that there was no sale or purchase transaction carried by assessee-company on NSEL during relevant assessment year and since there was no question of any income arising in hands of assessee resulting into escapement thereof, assumption of jurisdiction by Assessing Officer to reopen assessment was without any basis and, therefore, notice issued under section 148 was to be set aside - Whether since there was delay of 122 days in filing SLP which had not been satisfactorily explained, SLP filed by revenue was to be dismissed both on ground of delay as well as on merits - Held, yes[Paras 2 and 3][In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : SLP dismissed against order of High Court that where Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148 only on basis of information received from NSEL that assessee had received certain amount against sale of commodities but failed to deliver commodities or repayment of said amount, since such belief of Assessing Officer was without considering fact on record that there was no sale or purchase transaction carried by assessee-company on NSEL during relevant assessment year, impugned notice was without jurisdiction and was to be quashed

I. Section  148  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Issue of notice for  (Illustrations) - Assessment years  2010-11 and 2011-12  - High Court held that reasons for re-opening clearly went to show that Assessing Officer, except borrowing information from third report of Justice M.B. Shah Commission, failed to record independently to his own satisfaction any reason so as to direct re-opening of assessment, reopening was not permissible - Whether there was gross delay of 411 days in filing SLP which had not been satisfactorily explained and there was not good ground to interfere with impugned order and, thus, SLP filed was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section 148A, read with sections 148 and 149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section 3 of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 – Income escaping assessment - Conducting inquiry, providing opportunity before issue of notice (Limitation period) - Assessment year 2013-14 - Assessee challenged notice issued under section 148 on ground that it was time-barred as per newly substituted section 149(1)(a)  (b)- Revenue contended that time limit for issuing notice was extended until 30-6-2021, was extended by section 3 of TOLA read with Notification No. 20/2021 dated 31-3-2021, and Notification No. 38/2021 dated 27-4-2021, until 30-6-2021 - High Court by impugned order held that since time period for issuance of reassessment notice stood extended until 30-6-2021 and income alleged escaped income was over Rs. 50 lakhs, first proviso of section 149 would not be applicable - It further held that even without benefit of Instruction No. 01/2022 reopening notice issued on 23-6-2021 was within limitation - Whether since no interference was called for in order passed by High Court, SLP filed by assessee was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Para 3] [In favour of revenue]  Circulars  Notifications : Notification No. 20/2021 dated 31-3-2021, Notification No. 38/2021 dated 27-4-2021 and Instruction No. 1/2022, dated 11-5-2022.

Section  151,  read with sections  148  and  149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Sanction for issue of notice  (Specified Authority) - Assessment year  2019-20  - Assessee challenged initiation of reassessment proceedings on ground that sanction for initiation of reassessment should be granted by Principal Chief Commissioner - It was noted from section 151 approval form that case was covered under section 149(1)(b) (beyond three years but not more than ten years) - However, Assessing Officer proceeded after obtaining administrative approval under section 151 from Commissioner with approval granted on 27-4-2023 - High Court held that since approval was granted after expiry of 3 years from end of relevant assessment year, Commissioner should have realized that it was more than three years after expiry of assessment year, which was 2019-2020 and if some time had to be excluded as per fifth proviso to section 149, that should have been mentioned in order-sheet, otherwise it would only amount to exercising jurisdiction which he never had - Thus, impugned order passed under section 148A(d) and impugned notice issued under section 148 were to be quashed - Whether since there was gross delay of 411 days in filing SLP which had not been satisfactorily explained by revenue and, thus, SLP filed by revenue was to be dismissed on ground of delay as well as merits - Held, yes [Paras 1 to 3] [In favour of assessee]

Section  149,  read with section  148,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and section 3 of the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation of Certain Provisions) Ordinance, 2020 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice  (TOLA Scheme) - Assessment year  2013-14  - Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148 (old regime) on 28-6-2021 during extended time period as per TOLA - Pursuant to directions of Supreme Court, Assessing Officer provided information on 28-5-2022 and assessee filed reply on 11-6-2022 - Thereafter, order under section 148A(d) as well as notice under amended section 148 was issued on 27-7-2022 - Whether considering date of earlier notice under section 148 read with TOLA up to 30-06-2021, last permissible date for issuance of reassessment notice under section 148 would be 18-06-2022 - Held, yes - Whether thus, impugned notice dated 27-07-2022 issued under section 148 having been issued beyond surviving time would be invalid notice - Held, yes [Paras 7 and 10] [In favour of assessee]

Section 68, read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Cash Credits (Bogus sales) - Assessment year 2014-15 - Assessing Officer completed assessment of assessee under section 143(3) after considering special audit report - Later, Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148 on basis of information received from NSEL that certain amount was outstanding payable by assessee as on termination of trading activity on NSEL and assessee had received said amount against sale of commodities but failed to deliver commodities or repayment of said amount and, thus there was no actual sale done by assessee and by making such bogus sales assessee had benefitted and accordingly there was an escapement of income - High Court by impugned order held that since Assessing Officer issued impugned notice only on basis of information received from NSEL without considering facts on record to effect that there was no sale or purchase transaction carried by assessee-company on NSEL during relevant assessment year and since there was no question of any income arising in hands of assessee resulting into escapement thereof, assumption of jurisdiction by Assessing Officer to reopen assessment was without any basis and, therefore, notice issued under section 148 was to be set aside - Whether since there was delay of 122 days in filing SLP which had not been satisfactorily explained, SLP filed by revenue was to be dismissed both on ground of delay as well as on merits - Held, yes[Paras 2 and 3][In favour of assessee]

facts.text:
■

The assessee filed a return for AY 2015-16 declaring income of about Rs. 66.49 lakhs. Based on information that immovable properties were sold for about Rs. 1.89 crores against stamp duty value of about Rs. 16.08 crores, the case was reopened under section 147 after obtaining prior approval.

■

An original notice under section 148 was issued on 29-6-2021 under the unamended provisions. Pursuant to Supreme Court ruling in UOI v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC), the notice was treated as one under section 148A, an order under section 148A(d) was passed, a fresh notice under section 148 was issued on 29-7-2022, and reassessment was completed on 19-5-2023.

■

On appeal, the CIT(A) quashed the reassessment holding that reopening for assessment year 2015-16 was barred by limitation in view of UOI v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/469 ITR 46/301 Taxman 238 (SC), holding that TOLA applied only where limitation fell between 20-3-2020 and 31-3-2021.

■

On appeal by revenue to the Tribunal.

■

The assessee filed the return of income for the assessment year 2016–17 on 29-07-2016. A notice under section 148 was issued on 30-06-2021 under the old regime, taking benefit of the extended limitation provided by the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 (TOLA). Pursuant to decision of Supreme Court in case of Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1, the said notice dated 30-06-2021 was treated as a notice under section 148A(b) of the new regime, and accordingly, a fresh notice dated 24-5-2022 under section 148A(b) was issued by the Assessing Officer.

■

Thereafter, the Assessing Officer passed an order under section 148A(d) dated 15-7-2022, alleging that income of Rs.15.60 lakh had escaped assessment. On the same day, a fresh notice under section 148 was also issued.

■

The assessee challenged both the order under section 148A(d) and the notice under section 148 before the High Court, contending that they were issued beyond the permissible time limit.

■

It was submitted that, as held by the Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46, the reassessment notice dated 30-06-2021 (issued under the TOLA extension) would only be valid if the subsequent notice under section 148 was issued within the remaining time available under section 149.

■

Since only one day of limitation remained for issuing the section 148 notice, and the assessee was granted 14 days to respond from the date of the Ashish Agarwal judgment (21-05-2022), the last permissible date to issue notice was 12-6-2022.

■

As the impugned notice under section 148 was issued on 15-7-2022, the assessee submitted that it was time-barred, and consequently, the original notice dated 30-06-2021 and all proceedings thereafter were invalid.

For the assessment year 1966-67, assessment was reopened under section 148 by the ITO in the case of assessee, an individual. In the reassessment, the ITO included certain amount as unexplained investment in the income assessed earlier in the original assessment. The notice under section 148 was issued on 29-3-1975 but it was served on the assessee on 7-4-1975. On appeal before the AAC, the assessee contended that the notice having been served after the expiry of period of limitation, the reassessment proceedings were barred by limitation. The AAC rejected the assessee's contention. On second appeal, the Tribunal held that the notice under section 148 was not only to be issued but served within the period of limitation as laid down in section 149, and since the notice was served on the assessee after the expiry of 8 years, the order of reassessment was set aside.

On reference:

■

The Assessing Officers had issued notices under the erstwhile section 148 between 1-4-2021 and 30-6-2021 purportedly relying upon the relaxations under the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020 (TOLA). These notices were, later on, treated to be notices issued under section 148A(b) in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in Union of India v. Ashish Agrawal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC).

■

Subsequently, reply and objections were submitted by assessees and orders under section 148A(d) were passed which further led to issuance of fresh notices under section 148.

■

The assessees in all these cases had challenged the impugned notices issued under section 148 and the preceding orders under section 148A(d) primarily on ground that the reassessment proceedings were barred by limitation under the amended provisions of section 149 as inserted by the Finance Act, 2021 and clarified by the Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC).

For the assessment year 1961-62, a notice under section 148 was issued and despatched on 24-2-1970. No return was filed in response thereto. Therefore, the Assessing Officer issued another notice on 10-10-1973 under section 142(1) intimating to the assessee to appear on 23-11-1973. The assessee filed a reply to this notice stating that the alleged notice under section 148 was not served upon him and no proceedings under section 148 could be maintained against him as notice was not served upon him within 8 years. However, on 13-5-1974, an assessment order under section 144 was passed. By filing writ petition the assessee challenged the reassessment order. The High Court held that notice issued before limitation, if served on the assessee after limitation, would be void and ineffective but since an appeal was pending against the order of assessment, the High Court directed that the appeal be decided by the appellate authority in accordance with law.

On appeal to the Supreme Court:

For initiating reassessment proceedings under sections 147 and 148, the ITO sent a notice for reassessment which was actually signed by him on 30-3-1970 but was admittedly issued by registered post on 31-3-1970 to the assessee. The assessee was actually served with the notice later in the first week of April 1970. She contended that the notice, though issued within the limitation period, had not been served within eight years from the end of the relevant assessment year and was, hence, illegal and without jurisdiction. The ITO rejected this contention and made a best judgment assessment under section 144. He also initiated penalty proceedings and imposed penalty under section 271(1)(a). The AAC rejected the assessee's appeals. On further appeal, the Tribunal purportedly, following the Supreme Court's judgment in the case of Banarsi Debi v. ITO [1964] 53 ITR 100, annulled the reassessment as also the penalty proceedings on the ground that a notice of reassessment issued against the assessee before the limitation date prescribed under section 149 but served on the assessee after such date would be without jurisdiction and, thus, void and inoperative.

On reference:

For the assessment year 1995-96, the Assessing Officer completed the assessment of the assessee under section 143(3) on 28-2-2001 and it was found that the transaction of the assessee in the name of one ‘M’ showing trade deposit during assessment year 1994-95 of Rs. 4 lakhs and interest of Rs. 28,110 claimed to have been paid to it was bogus. The Assessing Officer, therefore, reopened the assessment of the assessee for the assessment year 1994-95 by issuing a notice under section 148 on 28-3-2001 and in reassessment proceedings, treated the deposit of Rs. 4 lakhs along with interest of Rs. 28,110 as income of the assessee under section 68.

On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) held that the notice under section 148 having been issued on 28-3-2001 after expiry of period of 4 years from the end of relevant assessment year 1994-95 was barred by limitation as per proviso to section 147 and notice under section 148 if so warranted could have been issued on or before 31-3-1999. He, therefore, annulled the reassessment order made by the Assessing Officer.

On revenue’s appeal :

■

The assessee was an individual and advocate by profession. For the year under consideration, the assessee did not file her return of income. Subsequently, on the basis of the information available on AIR/ITS, it was found that as per Form 26AS, the assessee received Rs. 52.22 lakhs as fees for professional services rendered for the year under consideration, however, the same was not disclosed as the return of income itself was not filed by the assessee.

■

Accordingly, on the basis of the aforesaid information, the Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148 on 29-6-2021. Subsequently, in view of the decision of the Supreme Court in Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC), original notice issued under section 148 on 29-6-2021 was deemed to be issued under section 148A(b).

■

After rejecting the objections filed by the assessee, an order under section 148A(d) was passed on 28-7-2022 declaring that it was a fit case for issuance of notice under section 148. Thereafter, on 28-7-2022, notice under section 148 was issued by the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer. In response to the notice issued under section 148, the assessee filed her return of income on 9-8-2022, declaring a total income of certain amount. The assessment order was passed under section 147 read with section 144B, assessing the total income of the assessee at certain amount after disallowing 20 per cent of the total expenditure claimed by the assessee.

■

On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) also upheld the addition made by the Assessing Officer.

■

On appeal to the Tribunal, the assessee submitted that for the year under consideration, the limitation period available with the Assessing Officer under section 149 for issuance of notice under section 148 was till 31-3-2020, and even if the extension granted by the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation and Amendment of Certain Provisions) Act, 2020, in light of the decision of the Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC), was considered, the Assessing Officer had time only till 26-6-2022 to issue notice under section 148. Therefore, the notice issued under section 148 on 28-7-2022 for the assessment year 2013-14 was barred by limitation. Hence, the entire reassessment proceedings culminating in the order passed under section 147 read with section 144B was void ab initio.

The notice dated 5-1-1962 issued under section 34(1)(a ) of the 1922 Act, seeking to reopen the assessment for the assessment year 1946-47, was quashed by the High Court as being barred by limitation. Thereafter, with the coming into force of the 1961 Act, the ITO issued a notice on 26-3-1963 under section 148 in respect of the said assessment. The High Court, on a writ petition filed by the assessee, again quashed the notice on the ground that the ITO was not competent to issue the same.

On appeal to the Supreme Court :

For the assessment year 1971-72 the assessee, a limited company, filed a return on the basis of which an order of assessment was made on 27-3-1974 and certain losses disclosed by the assessee were accepted. A notice under section 148 was issued to the assessee-company on 21-2-1976, pursuant to which the assessee-company filed a return on 27-3-1976 disclosing further losses. Till September 1981 no orders were passed in the reassessment proceedings. On writ, the High Court dismissed the writ petition filed by the assessee for the issuance of a mandamus to the ITO to pass orders in pursuance of the notice, observing that no such mandamus could be issued to ITO to make an order of assessment beyond the period of limitation prescribed by section 153(2).

On appeal to the Supreme Court:

■

The Assessing Officer issued a notice under section 148 for assessment year 2014-15 on 28-6-2021. The said notice was unsustainable as it was issued in accordance with the statutory regime as existed prior to 31-3-2021. Some High Courts struck down notices that were issued under section 148 after 31-3-2021 but under the unamended provisions relating to the re-assessment of income that had escaped assessment.

■

The revenue appealed the decisions rendered by various High Courts to the Supreme Court of India. In Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC)which was one of such appeals arising from the decision of the Allahabad High Court - the Supreme Court delivered its decision on 4-5-2022, whereby it concurred with the view that the amended provisions which came into force after 31-3-2021 would be applicable to notices issued thereafter.

■

However, the Supreme Court also issued certain directions in exercise of powers under article 142 of the Constitution of India. The Court directed that all notices that were issued under section 148 after 1-4-2021 till the date of the said decision (4-5-2022), including those that had been set aside by the High Courts, would be construed as show cause notices under section 148A(b).

■

The Assessing Officers were directed to provide the information and material relied upon by the revenue for issuance of such notices, to the respective assessees within a period of thirty days from the date of the decision so as to enable the respective assessees to respond to the same.

■

In compliance with the directions issued by the Supreme Court in the case of Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal (supra), the Assessing Officer provided information and material to the assessee on 30-5-2022. The assessee was granted two weeks' time to respond to the said notice.

■

The assessee responded to the notice dated 30-5-2022 on 11-6-2022. The Assessing Officer passed an order under section 148A(d) on 31-8-2022. According to the assessee, the same was beyond the period as stipulated.

■

On writ:

For the assessment year 1960-61, notice under section 148 was issued to the assessee on 28-3-1989. This notice was served upon the assessee on 1-4-1969. Following the judgment of this Court in Tikka Kushwant Singh v. CIT [1975] 101 ITR 106 , the Tribunal held the reassessment proceedings to be barred by time as issuance of notice under section 148 was also held to mean service of that notice upon the assessee.

On reference:

■

The Assessing Officer issued notice dated 28-6-2021 under section 148 for the assessment year 2013-14 during the extended period permitted under the Taxation and Other Laws (Relaxation of Certain Provisions) Ordinance, 2020 [(2020) 422 ITR (St.) 116] (TOLA).

■

In view of the ruling of the Supreme Court in Union of India v. Ashish Agarwal [2022] 138 taxmann.com 64/286 Taxman 183/444 ITR 1 (SC), such notice was deemed to be notice under section 148A(b), which came into the statute with effect from 1-4-2021. Thereafter, the Supreme Court in Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC) held that such notices would be valid or invalid depending upon the “surviving time” available between the date of issuance of notice under section 148 read with section 3(1) of TOLA up to 30-6-2021, and the issuance of notice under section 148 in terms of the directions in Ashish Agarwal (supra).

■

Thereafter, the Assessing Officer provided information to the assessee under section 148A(b) on 23-5-2022. Considering the statutory period of 15 days, the due date for filing reply was 6-6-2022. The assessee filed reply belatedly on 20-6-2022.

■

The Assessing Officer thereafter passed order under section 148A(d) and issued reassessment notice under section 148 on 29-7-2022.

■

The assessee filed instant writ petition and contended that reckoning limitation from the date of issuance of the original notice under section 148 read with TOLA up to 30-6-2021, and applying the ratio of Ashish Agarwal (supra) and Rajeev Bansal (supra), the “surviving time” available for valid issuance of notice expired on 13-6-2022. Consequently, the notice dated 29-7-2022 was issued beyond limitation.

■

The assessee filed his return of income on 25-9-2015 declaring total income at Rs. 15.93 lakhs. The Assessing Officer on the basis of information that assessee had a suspicious transactions related to long term gain of Rs. 56.69 lakhs through RIL, penny stock company engaged in facilitating bogus LTCG and, therefore, reassessment proceedings under section 147 were initiated and notice under section 148 was issued on 13-4-2021.

■

Thereafter, the notice issued under section 148 dated 13-4-2021 was treated as notice under section 148A(a) and information was supplied under section 148A(b). After considering the submissions of assessee, order under section 148A(d) was passed and, thereafter, notice under section 148 was issued on 18-7-2022.

■
